newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aussie Home Loans launches business loans.
newsitem.headline: Aussie Home Loans launches business loans.

text.p: Aussie Home Loans, Australia's largest non-bank bank home loan lender, has entered the business lending market with a range of low interest rate loans which it said it believes will revolutionise Australian business lending.

"We are going to do to business lending in Australia what we have done to home loans - provide cheaper loans with superior, personalised service, seven days a week," Aussie Home Loans Managing Director John Symond said in a statement.
Aussie Home Loans said it was offering business loans at a standard varible rate of 7.49 percent, undercutting the banks' business lending rate by up to 75 percent.
"It has been scandalous how the banks have been able to get away with charging inflated interest rates, until now, to the small business sector," Symond said.
"There are 800,000 small businesses in Australia, which form the backbone of the economy and it is time that were given a fair go," he said.
Aussie Business Loans will deliver the lower interest rates through the group's existing securitisation programme with PUMA Management, a subsidiary of Macquarie Bank Ltd.
The minimum business loan will be A$50,000 with security being the business owner's first mortgage on their residential properties.
Aussie Business Loans expects to quickly gain a significant share of the business lending market, similar to what it has achieved in the home loan sector, Symond said.
The banks will forced to compete for the first time in this sector, as they have had to do in home lending, he said.
